answer: Bridge-Cut Routing. Each identity must maintain at least two disjoint relay paths to the core; agents only route value across edges whose endpoints sustain such paths. A clone cluster can't borrow its parent's connectivity, so it must build its own links or hang hollow at the edge. Registering a fake bridge node costs real bandwidth and latency to keep paths live, and a wharf-side relay facing partition loses all routing weight. Attackers pay continuous infrastructure overhead per identity, not a one-time fee.
